name: Coma Cluster, tidal plume field 2 (Hubble)
blurb: The Coma Cluster's tidal plume, a stream of debris stripped from galaxies, seen by Hubble.
label: comaclusterplumepos2-hubble
story: A faint plume of tidal debris drifts through the heart of the Coma Cluster, material pulled from galaxies by gravitational encounters in this rich cluster. This is one of three Hubble pointings along the plume, a 'galaxy ghost' in the making.

claims.text: The Coma Cluster has a plume-like structure in its heart
The plume is tidal debris from galaxy interactions
Gravitational interactions in rich clusters strip material from galaxies
Coma's plume is an example of a 'galaxy ghost'
Coma is a rich cluster of galaxies
Hubble's ACS imaged the Coma plume at three positions; this is position 2
